SMTO-MEM-0019 — Search data for your memories isn't there yet

GUID: 711e2ef5-d3b3-53fe-86b5-bdcb5c8514cd
Slug: knowledge-index-missing
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • SMTO has no search data for your memories under the current Knowledge settings. Your saved memories are kept; until the search data is rebuilt, SMTO finds them by simple keyword matching.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Knowledge › Semantic memory and watch the Memory index status. SMTO starts rebuilding missing Memory search data by itself, and the progress bar shows how far it has got.
  2. If the status shows Memory indexing needs attention or doesn't move, select Retry Memory indexing, or Rebuild Memory index below the settings. Both start a fresh build of the search data from your saved memories.
  3. If the rebuild fails with an error about the embeddings model, follow that error's steps first. Rebuilding needs the embeddings model to be working.

What success looks like

  • The Memory status in Knowledge › Semantic memory shows Memory index is up to date.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete memories or documents to clear this; the search data is rebuilt from them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Vector search found no index collection for the requested lane and embedding profile (index_missing); Memory recall degrades to keyword matching and a forced Memory backfill is queued.

What this means

  • The source has no search data for the selected configuration. Its original content may still be available. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported index_missing. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The affected source or Memory index reaches Ready.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the vector database is running and whether the Memory collection for the current profile exists. Let the forced Memory backfill finish, or start it with Rebuild Memory index or Retry Memory indexing. Do not delete stored memories; the index is rebuilt from them.
  • Open Knowledge, select the affected source and choose Manage → Reindex. For Memory, use Retry Memory indexing.

Retry and execution caution

  • The affected source or Memory index reaches Ready.

How to verify the fix

  • The affected source or Memory index reaches Ready.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
